text:
The correct decreasing order of energy for the orbitals having, following set of quantum numbers :

(A) n = 3, l = 0, m = 0

(B) n = 4, l = 0, m = 0

(C) n = 3, l = 1, m = 0

(D) n = 3, l = 2, m = 1

is :
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2022 (Online) 27th July Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
(A) $\mathrm{n}+\ell =3+0=3$

(B) $\mathrm{n}+\ell =4+0=4$

(C) $\mathrm{n}+\ell =3+1=4$

(D) $\mathrm{n}+\ell =3+2=5$

Higher $\mathrm{n}+\ell$ value, higher the energy & if same $\mathrm{n}+\ell$ value, then higher $\mathrm{n}$ value, higher the energy.

Thus : $\mathrm{D}>\mathrm{B}>\mathrm{C}>\mathrm{A}$.

text: The plot of $\mathrm{pH}$-metric titration of weak base $\mathrm{NH}_{4}\mathrm{OH}$ vs strong acid HCl looks like :
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2022 (Online) 27th July Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Here $\mathrm{HCl}$ is added to $\mathrm{NH}{}_{4}\mathrm{OH}$, so the pH starts above 7 and falls as acid is added; curves (B) and (D), in which the pH rises, are excluded.

Before the equivalence point the solution contains $\mathrm{NH}{}_{4}\mathrm{OH}$ and $\mathrm{NH}{}_{4}\mathrm{Cl}$, a basic buffer, so the pH falls only gradually.

At the equivalence point only $\mathrm{NH}{}_{4}\mathrm{Cl}$ is present, and its cation hydrolyses ($\mathrm{NH}{}_{4}{}^{+}+\mathrm{H}{}_{2}\mathrm{O}\mathrm{NH}{}_{4}\mathrm{OH}+\mathrm{H}{}^{+}$), so the equivalence point lies below pH 7 and the jump around it is small; afterwards excess $\mathrm{HCl}$ keeps the pH low.

Curve (A), a gradual fall with a short drop centred below pH 7, matches. Curve (C), a long, almost vertical drop across pH 7, is the shape for a strong base titrated with a strong acid.

Hence, the correct option is (A).
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2022 (Online) 27th July Evening Shift

text: An organic compound ${}^{'}\mathrm{A}^{'}$ contains nitrogen and chlorine. It dissolves readily in water to give a solution that turns litmus red. Titration of compound ${}^{'}\mathrm{A}^{'}$ with standard base indicates that the molecular weight of ${}^{'}\mathrm{A}^{'}$ is $131\pm 2$. When a sample of ${}^{'}\mathrm{A}^{'}$ is treated with aq. $\mathrm{NaOH}$, a liquid separates which contains $\mathrm{N}$ but not $\mathrm{Cl}$. Treatment of the obtained liquid with nitrous acid followed by phenol gives orange precipitate. The compound ${}^{'}\mathrm{A}^{'}$ is :
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2022 (Online) 27th July Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Compound A is acidic in water, contains N and Cl, and with aq. NaOH gives a liquid amine that contains N but not Cl, so A is the hydrochloride salt of an amine:

$\mathrm{RNH}{}_{3}{}^{+}\mathrm{Cl}{}^{-}+\mathrm{NaOH}\longrightarrow \mathrm{RNH}{}_{2}+\mathrm{NaCl}+\mathrm{H}{}_{2}\mathrm{O}$

The liberated amine gives an orange azo dye with nitrous acid followed by phenol, so it is an aromatic primary amine: only an arenediazonium salt is stable enough to couple with phenol. The amine is aniline and A is anilinium chloride.


[IMG]

For $\mathrm{C}{}_{6}\mathrm{H}{}_{5}\mathrm{NH}{}_{3}{}^{+}\mathrm{Cl}{}^{-}$, $M=72+8+14+35.5=129.5$, which lies within $131\pm 2$.

In (A) and (C) the nitrogen is bonded to an sp³ carbon, so the freed amines are aliphatic primary amines whose diazonium salts lose $\mathrm{N}{}_{2}$ and give no azo dye; (B) is a free chloroaniline, not a salt, and its liquid would contain Cl.

Hence, the correct option is (D).
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2022 (Online) 27th July Evening Shift

text:
Match List - I with List - II.

  
    
    List - I
(Mixture)
    
    List - II
(Purification Process)
  

  
    (A)
    Chloroform & Aniline
    (I)
    Steam distillation
  
  
    (B)
    Benzoic acid & Naphthalene
    (II)
    Sublimation
  
  
    (C)
    Water & Aniline
    (III)
    Distillation
  
  
    (D)
    Naphthalene & Sodium chloride
    (IV)
    Crystallisation
  

Choose the correct answer from the options given below :
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2022 (Online) 27th July Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
(A) Chloroform (b.p. 334 K) and aniline (b.p. 457 K) are miscible liquids with widely different boiling points, so simple distillation separates them: (III).

(B) Benzoic acid and naphthalene both sublime, so sublimation cannot separate them; benzoic acid dissolves in hot water while naphthalene does not, so they are separated by crystallisation: (IV).

(C) Aniline is steam-volatile and immiscible with water, so it is separated from water by steam distillation: (I).

(D) Naphthalene sublimes on heating while sodium chloride does not, so they are separated by sublimation: (II).

Hence, the correct option is (D).
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2022 (Online) 27th July Evening Shift

text: The normality of $\mathrm{H}_{2}\mathrm{SO}_{4}$ in the solution obtained on mixing $100\mathrm{mL}$ of $0.1\mathrm{M}\mathrm{H}_{2}\mathrm{SO}_{4}$ with $50\mathrm{mL}$ of $0.1\mathrm{M}\mathrm{NaOH}$ is $_______________$ $\times 10^{-1}\mathrm{N}$. (Nearest Integer)
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2022 (Online) 27th July Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
No. of equivalents of $\mathrm{H}_{2}\mathrm{SO}_{4}=100\times 0.1\times 2=20$

No. of equivalents of $\mathrm{NaOH}=50\times 0.1=5$

No. of equivalents of $\mathrm{H}_{2}\mathrm{SO}_{4}$ left $=20-5=15$

$\begin{array}{l} \Rightarrow 150\times \mathrm{x}=15 \\  \\ \mathrm{x}=\dfrac{1}{10}=0.1\mathrm{N}=1\times 10^{-1}\mathrm{N} \end{array}$

text: A gas (Molar mass = 280 $\mathrm{g}\mathrm{mol}^{-1}$) was burnt in excess $\mathrm{O}_{2}$ in a constant volume calorimeter and during combustion the temperature of calorimeter increased from $298.0\mathrm{K}$ to $298.45$ $\mathrm{K}$. If the heat capacity of calorimeter is $2.5\mathrm{kJ}\mathrm{K}^{-1}$ and enthalpy of combustion of gas is $9\mathrm{kJ}\mathrm{mol}^{-1}$ then amount of gas burnt is $_____________ g. ($Nearest Integer)
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2022 (Online) 27th July Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
$\Delta \mathrm{U}=\mathrm{C}\Delta \mathrm{T}$

$\begin{array}{l} =2.5\times 10^{3}\times 0.45 \\  \\ =1.125\mathrm{kJ} \end{array}$

Considering $\Delta \mathrm{H}\simeq \Delta \mathrm{U}$

$\Delta \mathrm{H}=9\mathrm{kJ}/\mathrm{mol}\simeq \Delta \mathrm{U}$

$\therefore$ Mass of gas burnt $=\frac{1.125}{9}\times 280=35\mathrm{g}$
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2022 (Online) 27th July Evening Shift

text: When a certain amount of solid A is dissolved in $100\mathrm{g}$ of water at $25^{\circ }\mathrm{C}$ to make a dilute solution, the vapour pressure of the solution is reduced to one-half of that of pure water. The vapour pressure of pure water is $23.76\mathrm{mmHg}$. The number of moles of solute A added is $_____________. ($Nearest Integer)
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2022 (Online) 27th July Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
$\because$ Dilute solution given:

$\frac{\mathrm{P}^{0}-\mathrm{P}_{\mathrm{S}}}{\mathrm{P}^{0}}\sim \frac{{}^{\mathrm{n}}\text{solute}}{{}^{\mathrm{n}}\text{solvent}}$

$\frac{\mathrm{P}^{0}-\mathrm{P}^{0}/2}{\mathrm{P}^{0}}=\frac{{}^{\mathrm{n}}\text{solute}}{{}^{\mathrm{n}}\text{solvent}}$

${}^{\mathrm{n}}$ solute $\sim \frac{{}^{\mathrm{n}}\text{solvent}}{2}=\frac{100}{18\times 2}=2.78\mathrm{mol}$

More accurate approach:

$\frac{\mathrm{P}^{0}-\mathrm{P}_{\mathrm{S}}}{\mathrm{P}_{\mathrm{S}}}=\frac{{}^{\mathrm{n}}\text{solute}}{{}^{\mathrm{n}}\text{solvent}}$

$\frac{\mathrm{P}^{0}-\mathrm{P}^{0}/2}{\mathrm{P}^{0}/2}=\frac{{}^{\mathrm{n}}\text{solute}}{{}^{n}\text{solvent}}$

${}^{n}$ solute $={}^{n}$ solvent $=\frac{100}{18}=5.55\mathrm{mol}$
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2022 (Online) 27th July Evening Shift

text:
The number of molecule(s) or ion(s) from the following having non-planar structure is $____________$.

$\mathrm{NO}_{3}^{-},\mathrm{H}_{2}\mathrm{O}_{2},\mathrm{BF}_{3},\mathrm{PCl}_{3},\mathrm{XeF}_{4},\mathrm{SF}_{4},\mathrm{XeO}_{3},\mathrm{PH}_{4}^{+},\mathrm{SO}_{3},[\mathrm{Al}(\mathrm{OH})_{4}]^{-}$
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2022 (Online) 27th July Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Shapes follow from VSEPR (bond pairs and lone pairs on the central atom).

Planar species: $\mathrm{NO}{}_{3}{}^{-}$ ($sp^{2}$, trigonal planar), $\mathrm{BF}{}_{3}$ ($sp^{2}$, trigonal planar), $\mathrm{SO}{}_{3}$ ($sp^{2}$, trigonal planar) and $\mathrm{XeF}{}_{4}$ ($sp^{3}d^{2}$, 4 bond pairs + 2 lone pairs, square planar).

Non-planar species: $\mathrm{H}{}_{2}\mathrm{O}{}_{2}$ (open-book structure, the two O–H bonds lie in different planes), $\mathrm{PCl}{}_{3}$ ($sp^{3}$, one lone pair, trigonal pyramidal), $\mathrm{SF}{}_{4}$ ($sp^{3}d$, one lone pair, see-saw), $\mathrm{XeO}{}_{3}$ ($sp^{3}$, one lone pair on Xe, trigonal pyramidal), $\mathrm{PH}{}_{4}{}^{+}$ ($sp^{3}$, tetrahedral) and $[\mathrm{Al}(\mathrm{OH}){}_{4}]{}^{-}$ ($sp^{3}$, tetrahedral).

Number of non-planar species $=6$.

Hence, the answer is 6.
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2022 (Online) 27th July Evening Shift
